rules.statement: Design every module other than Core so it can be enabled, disabled, or omitted independently of every other non-Core module; a dependency on Core is the only permitted module dependency, and a high-level module must never depend on another high-level module directly

Treat Core as the one mandatory module every tenant has enabled by default; it provides settings, theming, notifications, permissions, the organisation profile, outbound and inbound email, extension points, record metadata, module dependencies, terminology, dashboards, reporting, usage metering, and the shared customer directory as services that other modules consume only through events and DTOs, never through direct calls
Modules must never import or reference another module's classes directly; all cross-module data flows through events and typed DTOs

When one module's workflow should produce a side effect in another optional module, such as generating an invoice when a booking is confirmed, the source module dispatches a named event to Core's event bus rather than calling the other module directly; the target module reacts only if it is installed and enabled for that tenant, and the source module must keep working normally if no listener is present

Model a business entity shared by more than one module, such as customers or the tenant's own organisation profile, once in Core and reference it everywhere else by id; a module must never own its own duplicate copy of an entity another module also needs
Every cross-module payload must be a typed, immutable DTO class, never a raw array, generic object, or persistence model

Treat Core as an operating system and other modules as apps: Core exposes named extension points through CoreExtensionPoints that a module can register into; a module must never directly edit or reach into another module's UI or database schema

Give every module the ability to attach structured or semi-structured data to a Core record through CoreRecordExtensions rather than altering Core's schema, keeping Core's own tables clean and industry-agnostic

Declare a module's hard prerequisite modules explicitly in CoreModuleDependencyRegistry; never let a module assume another module is present without that dependency being declared and enforced by ModuleManager

Store every Core entity under its most generic, industry-neutral name internally, such as Party, Account, or Contact, and let CoreTerminology translate it into the vocabulary a tenant's business type expects, such as Customer, Patient, or Student, in the UI and on generated documents
Let each module register its own dashboard widgets with CoreDashboardRegistry and serve its own widget data from its own endpoint; the Core dashboard must never query another module's tables directly

Build cross-module reports through CoreReportingPipeline primarily via tenant-scoped, indexed, pre-aggregated summaries of each module's time-series data, since merging large multi-month datasets at the application layer scales poorly and risks memory exhaustion; reserve the application-layer merge for small result sets, and never build a cross-module report through a join across module-owned tables
Index every tenant-scoped table with a composite key that starts with tenant_id, such as (tenant_id, created_at) or (tenant_id, status), so queries narrow to the tenant before filtering further

Never hardcode a module's classification or category field as a rigid database enum when tenants or other modules may need to add, disable, or hide options; keep a small fixed enum only for a genuinely universal top-level classification, and put anything that must be modular, tenant-configured, or dependent on which modules are enabled into a relational, indexed lookup table instead
Scope every tenant-owned database table with a tenant_id column and apply an automatic application-level tenant filter to every query so queries are isolated per tenant

Never rely on the application-level tenant filter alone; it does not protect raw queries, direct table access, third-party package models, or a query that explicitly disables the filter. Enforce database-level row isolation on every tenant-owned table as the backstop, keyed on a per-request current-tenant identifier that TenantMiddleware sets on the database connection for every request, so the database itself refuses cross-tenant reads and writes regardless of application-layer bugs
Never allow a query, job, cache key, or file path to cross tenant boundaries without an explicit tenant_id check
Resolve the current tenant from the request hostname via a central TenantMiddleware before any tenant-scoped route executes, matching either the wildcard subdomain or a verified mapped custom domain

Scope every session cookie to the exact hostname the request arrived on, whether that is the tenant's platform subdomain or its verified custom_domain, and never to the shared parent domain, so session cookies and CSRF tokens establish correctly and are never sent to another tenant's hostname or to the control plane
Provision every new tenant on a wildcard subdomain of the form client-slug.pendagraphics.co.za by default, available instantly at signup with no DNS action required from the customer
Offer custom domain mapping (client-domain.co.za) on the Enterprise plan only, activated only after DNS ownership verification and never before
Gate module access by the tenant's active subscription plan rather than a cryptographically signed offline licence file

Define exactly three subscription plans, Starter, Professional, and Enterprise, each including the Core, Financial, and Support modules, so that plans differ only by usage limits and branding: Starter allows 2 workspace user seats, up to 50 support tickets per month, up to R50,000 (or USD 3,000) of payments processed per month, and a shared subdomain; Professional allows 10 workspace user seats, up to 500 support tickets per month, up to R500,000 (or USD 30,000) of payments processed per month, and a shared subdomain; Enterprise allows unlimited seats, tickets, and processed volume and is the only plan that may map a custom domain
Count only internal workspace users as user seats; customer portal users never consume a seat

Price every plan in two currencies, billing a tenant whose business is in South Africa in ZAR and every other tenant in USD: Starter costs R249 or USD 19 per month, Professional costs R699 or USD 49 per month, and Enterprise starts from R2,499 or USD 149 per month, with custom quotes above the starting price

Offer annual billing at a 20 percent discount charged upfront for the year, where the discounted monthly equivalent is 80 percent of the monthly price rounded down to a whole currency unit, for example Starter at R199 or USD 15 per month, and the annual charge is twelve times that equivalent

Measure plan limits per calendar month per tenant; the seat limit is a hard limit that rejects adding another active workspace user, while the processed-volume and support-ticket limits are soft limits that warn the tenant admin at 80 percent and at 100 percent of the allowance and prompt an upgrade; no limit may ever delete, hide, or reject data that a tenant's customers have already submitted

Define module-to-plan inclusion and per-tenant paid add-on entitlements as data rather than code, so that a future module can be bundled into selected plans or sold as an individually priced add-on to any plan without changing existing modules

Enforce signup uniqueness on the complete email address of a user and never on the email domain, so that several people from the same company or from a free email provider can each register their own tenant or account
Issue a TLS certificate only for a hostname that is an active tenant's platform subdomain or a verified custom domain, and never for an arbitrary or unverified hostname
Use a shared UI component library for all UI primitives; no module may reimplement a shared component, and every module's forms and ledgers must look and behave identically

Store third-party credentials, such as Paysharp, Paystack, Microsoft Graph, SMTP, PayStack, Stripe, and Chargebee secrets, encrypted per tenant, and never log raw card, account, or gateway secret details

Separate the control plane, which runs platform-wide tenant provisioning, the tenant directory, and the operator's own billing of tenants, from the data plane, which is the tenant-facing application made of the Core, Financial, and Support modules; the control plane must be served only from admin.pendagraphics.co.za and must never be reachable from a tenant's own subdomain or custom domain
Keep the operator's own billing of tenants for their subscription plan, run by the control plane's Billing Engine, entirely separate from the Financial module, which bills a tenant's own customers

Provide outbound email delivery as a Core service used by every module; default every tenant to the platform's own shared, pre-verified sending domain, and offer Microsoft 365 Admin Consent or a validated custom SMTP relay as tenant-owned delivery options on the Enterprise plan only

Never trust email threading headers such as In-Reply-To or References to match an inbound reply to its tenant-scoped record; they can be forged, stripped, or spoofed. Every outbound platform_shared email that expects a reply must embed a cryptographically signed token in its Reply-To sub-address, and CoreInboundEmailRouting must verify that signature before running any tenant lookup or matching logic against an inbound payload

Build each module's first release as an Enterprise-Ready MVP: implement only the MVP scope explicitly listed for that module, but shape its database tables, module boundaries, and DTOs so the deferred enterprise features can be added later without a breaking schema change or a violation of these architectural rules

For the Support module MVP, build only single web-form and email intake, relational dynamic categories, simple chronological ticket statuses, and core private notes with mentions; defer omnichannel chat and social intake, workload-based automated assignment, proactive SLA breach alerting, and automated knowledge-base deflection to a post-launch phase

features.name: TenantOnboarding
features.description: Self-service signup flow that instantly provisions a new tenant on a wildcard subdomain, replacing the offline installation wizard

actions.statement: Validate company_name, admin_email, and admin_password meet minimum requirements
Check admin_email is not already registered as a user of any tenant on the platform, comparing the complete email address and never the email domain

enforce.expression: Many users and tenants may share an email domain, including a free provider such as gmail.com; only an exact email address match counts as a duplicate

actions.statement: Normalise requested_subdomain to lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens only, falling back to a slug derived from company_name if left blank
Create a new Tenant record with a unique subdomain of the form requested_subdomain.pendagraphics.co.za

enforce.expression: The subdomain must be unique across all tenants and must not collide with a reserved system subdomain such as www, api, admin, app, mail, reply, control, or status

actions.statement: Capture business_type so CoreTerminology can resolve industry-specific display labels for this tenant
Determine the tenant's billing currency as ZAR when country_code is ZA and USD otherwise, and record it on the tenant
Provision tenant-scoped default settings, including the default colour palette and an empty organisation profile
Register the new tenant in the control plane's TenantRegistry with active status
Seed Core module data scoped to the new tenant
Create the tenant admin user and assign the Tenant Admin role
Activate the selected subscription_plan with the chosen billing_cycle and billing currency through the PlatformBillingEngine, and enable the modules included in that plan
Send a welcome email with a link to the tenant's wildcard subdomain workspace

Issue a single-use, short-lived, cryptographically signed login handoff token for the new tenant admin and perform a full browser navigation, never a client-side in-app redirect, to the tenant's wildcard subdomain, where the token is redeemed to establish the admin's session on that hostname and land on the dashboard

enforce.expression: Crossing from the main platform site to a tenant's wildcard subdomain must use a full browser navigation so the browser cleanly re-establishes cookies and CSRF tokens across the domain boundary; a client-side in-app redirect must never be used to cross a hostname boundary
A login handoff token must expire within one minute, be redeemable exactly once, and be valid only for the tenant and user it was issued to
The workspace must be reachable on the wildcard subdomain immediately, with no manual DNS step required from the customer

features.name: SubscriptionManagement
features.description: Manages tenant subscription plans and gates module access accordingly, replacing RSA offline licence validation

actions.statement: Look up the tenant's current subscription record
Validate the requested plan change against the control plane's PlatformBillingEngine
Update the tenant's active plan and billing_cycle
Recompute the modules, user seats, monthly processed-volume allowance, monthly support-ticket allowance, and custom-domain entitlement allowed under the new plan

enforce.expression: A downgrade must not silently delete data belonging to a now-disabled module
A downgrade must be rejected while the tenant's active workspace user count exceeds the target plan's seat limit, telling the tenant admin how many users to deactivate first

actions.statement: Disable module routes for modules no longer included in the plan while preserving their underlying data
When a downgrade removes the custom-domain entitlement, deactivate routing for the custom domain while preserving its record and keeping the platform subdomain working
Notify the tenant admin of the plan change by email and in-app notification

features.name: CustomDomainMapping
features.description: Maps a tenant's own domain over their default wildcard subdomain, available on the Enterprise plan only, after DNS verification

actions.statement: Verify the tenant's active subscription plan includes custom domain mapping

enforce.expression: Only Enterprise tenants may add a custom domain; Starter and Professional tenants must remain on their shared platform subdomain

actions.statement: Generate a unique DNS verification token and a CNAME target pointing to the wildcard subdomain infrastructure
Store the custom_domain against the tenant in a pending, unverified state
Instruct the tenant admin to create the CNAME record and a TXT record containing the verification token at their DNS provider
Poll the domain's DNS records until the CNAME and TXT verification token are found

enforce.expression: The domain must not be marked verified until both the CNAME and TXT token checks pass

actions.statement: Issue and install an SSL certificate for the verified custom_domain

enforce.expression: A certificate must never be issued for a custom domain that is unverified, pending, or not mapped to an active tenant

actions.statement: Mark the custom_domain as active and route requests for that hostname to the tenant's workspace
Update the tenant's routing information in the control plane's TenantRegistry
Keep the original wildcard subdomain reachable and pointed at the same tenant after mapping

features.name: ModuleManager
features.description: Tenant-admin UI for enabling and disabling modules permitted by the active subscription plan and by declared module prerequisites

actions.statement: Verify module_key is included in the tenant's active subscription plan or has been purchased by the tenant as an add-on

enforce.expression: A module that is neither included in the current plan nor purchased as an add-on cannot be enabled
The Core module must always remain enabled for every tenant and can never be disabled through this feature

actions.statement: Look up module_key's declared prerequisites in CoreModuleDependencyRegistry

enforce.expression: A module cannot be enabled unless every module listed as its prerequisite is already enabled for the tenant
A module cannot be disabled while another currently enabled module still declares it as a prerequisite

actions.statement: Toggle the module's enabled flag for this tenant only
Run the module's migrations and seeders scoped to this tenant if enabling for the first time
Deregister the module's CoreExtensionPoints hooks and CoreDashboardRegistry widgets if it was just disabled
Refresh the tenant's cached active-modules list used for route gating and sidebar navigation

features.name: AuthenticationAndAccess
features.description: Tenant-scoped authentication with two guards: internal workspace users and customer portal users

actions.statement: Resolve the tenant from the request hostname, matching it against the wildcard subdomain pattern or a verified mapped custom domain, before attempting authentication

enforce.expression: An unverified or pending custom domain must never resolve to a tenant

actions.statement: Set the resolved tenant_id as the current-tenant identifier on the database connection for the lifetime of the request, so database-level row isolation enforces tenant isolation independently of the application-level tenant filter

enforce.expression: A request must never reach a tenant-scoped query without the current-tenant identifier having been set on that connection first

actions.statement: Authenticate the user against the resolved tenant's user pool only

enforce.expression: A user record belonging to a different tenant must never authenticate against this tenant's session

actions.statement: Regenerate the session ID on successful login to prevent session fixation
Load the user's roles and permissions scoped to the current tenant
Share auth.user, auth.permissions, and the tenant's active modules with the frontend as global shared state on every subsequent request

features.name: TenantRegistry
features.description: Control plane: the operator-facing directory of every tenant, recording metadata, active or suspended status, database routing, and a pointer to that tenant's CoreOrganisationProfile

actions.statement: Record the tenant's subdomain, mapped custom domain if any, and database_connection routing information, which points every tenant at the single shared platform database by default while allowing a tenant to be routed elsewhere later without a schema change
Reflect the tenant's current status as active, suspended, or cancelled
Suspend a tenant's data-plane access immediately when status changes to suspended, without deleting their data

enforce.expression: A suspended tenant's workspace and portal routes must return a clear suspended-account response rather than partial access

actions.statement: Expose the registry to the control plane's TenantMiddleware so tenant resolution and database routing stay in sync

features.name: PlatformBillingEngine
features.description: Control plane: the SaaS operator's own billing of tenants for their subscription plan, integrated with a payment processor such as Paystack

actions.statement: Create or update the tenant's subscription record with the connected processor

Price the subscription from the plan catalogue using the tenant's billing_currency and billing_cycle, applying the annual discount when billing_cycle is annual and handling Enterprise as a starting price with custom quotes above it
Handle plan changes, renewals, and payment failures reported by the processor via webhook

enforce.expression: A processor webhook must be signature-verified before it can change any tenant's subscription state

actions.statement: Trigger SubscriptionManagement to recompute allowed modules, seats, and usage allowances when the processor confirms a plan change
Mark the tenant Past Due and notify the tenant admin after a failed renewal, before suspending access in TenantRegistry
Generate the operator's own invoice to the tenant for each billing cycle

features.name: PlatformSupportDesk
features.description: Control plane: internal support ticketing the SaaS operator's own staff use to resolve issues raised by tenant accounts, distinct from the tenant-facing Support module tenants use for their own customers

actions.statement: Create an operator-side ticket linked to the reporting tenant_id
Allow operator staff to view the tenant's TenantRegistry status and PlatformBillingEngine subscription details alongside the ticket for context
Track the ticket through New, In Progress, Pending, and Resolved statuses
Notify the tenant admin by email when the ticket status changes

features.name: CoreSettings
features.description: Core module: manages tenant-scoped and module-scoped key-value application settings that every other module reads through a shared Settings facade

actions.statement: Resolve the settings scope, either global to the tenant or namespaced to a specific module
Validate setting_key is registered for the resolved scope
Persist setting_value as a JSON-typed value under the resolved scope
Clear any cached settings for this tenant and scope
Broadcast a SettingsUpdated event carrying a typed SettingsUpdatedDTO so listening modules can react without direct coupling

features.name: CoreTheming
features.description: Core module: tenant-configurable colour palette applied instantly across the UI via CSS custom properties

actions.statement: Validate each submitted colour value is a well-formed hex code
Check the WCAG AA contrast ratio between text and background tokens

enforce.expression: Any token pair below a 4.5:1 contrast ratio must surface a warning before saving

actions.statement: Persist the palette to tenant-scoped settings under the theme group via CoreSettings
Return the updated theme to the frontend and apply it directly to the root layout through a reactive binding rather than only writing CSS custom properties as a side effect

enforce.expression: The theme must be applied through the frontend's own reactivity on the root layout binding, not only through a shared-state side effect, to avoid a flash of unstyled content or stale colours when a tenant admin updates the palette or a user switches tabs quickly

features.name: CoreNotifications
features.description: Core module: in-app, toast, and email notifications dispatched in response to events raised by any module

actions.statement: Resolve the notifying user's channel preferences for the given notification_type
Write the notification to the tenant-scoped notifications table

enforce.expression: A notification must never be written or delivered to a user outside the resolved tenant

actions.statement: Push an in-app toast if the user has an active session
Queue an email notification via CoreEmailIntegration if the user has enabled the email channel for this type

features.name: CorePermissions
features.description: Core module: tenant-scoped roles and permissions that every other module's policies enforce against

actions.statement: Validate permission_key follows the module.resource.action naming convention
Create or update the role scoped to the current tenant
Attach or detach the permission from the role

enforce.expression: A Super Admin role must always retain the wildcard permission and can never be edited or deleted

actions.statement: Refresh the cached permission set for every user assigned the role

features.name: CoreOrganisationProfile
features.description: Core module: the tenant's own organisation profile, used to brand every customer-facing document and screen across every other module

actions.statement: Validate organisation_name and organisation_email
Persist the organisation profile scoped to the tenant

enforce.expression: Only one organisation profile may exist per tenant

actions.statement: Accept and store an uploaded logo file for use across the app and on generated documents
Broadcast an OrganisationProfileUpdated event so Financial, Support, and other modules refresh cached copies of the letterhead details

features.name: CoreCustomerManagement
features.description: Core module: the single shared Party/Contact directory, stored under Core's generic industry-neutral schema and displayed as Customer, Patient, Student, or similar via CoreTerminology, that Financial, Support, and any future module reference by customer_id so every module stays in sync on the same record

actions.statement: Validate customer_name and email
Check whether a customer with this email already exists for the current tenant
Create or update the customer record, including billing_address and tax_number, scoped to the current tenant

enforce.expression: A customer record must never be created without a tenant_id scope
No other module may persist its own copy of customer name, email, phone, or address; it must store only the customer_id and read the rest from Core

actions.statement: Store the record under Core's generic Party/Contact schema regardless of the tenant's business_type; only the CoreTerminology display label changes
Dispatch a CustomerCreated or CustomerUpdated event carrying a typed CustomerDTO so listening modules can react without querying Core's tables directly

features.name: CoreEmailIntegration
features.description: Core module: configures how the tenant's outbound email is sent, from zero-setup shared delivery to the tenant's own Microsoft 365 or custom SMTP infrastructure on the Enterprise plan

actions.statement: Default every new tenant to platform_shared delivery through the platform's own verified sending domain, requiring zero setup
For microsoft365, let the tenant's IT administrator initiate a Microsoft Graph Admin Consent flow requesting application-level Mail.Send and Mail.Read permissions

enforce.expression: microsoft365 delivery must only be offered to tenants on the Enterprise plan

actions.statement: Store the resulting tenant-wide Microsoft Graph access token encrypted and scoped to this tenant only
For custom_smtp, accept a single relay credential set from the tenant's IT administrator and test the connection before saving

enforce.expression: A custom_smtp configuration must be successfully test-connected before it can be marked active

actions.statement: When sending any email on behalf of a workspace user, set the From header to that user's own address while authenticating through the tenant's configured provider

For any platform_shared email that expects a threaded reply, generate a cryptographically signed token binding the tenant_id and the originating record, and embed it in a Reply-To sub-address such as reply+ticket_abc123_signaturehash@reply.pendagraphics.co.za

enforce.expression: A signed Reply-To token must never be derived from guessable or sequential data; it must be a genuine cryptographic signature, in the style of signed URLs

actions.statement: Fall back to platform_shared delivery whenever a tenant's microsoft365 or custom_smtp configuration is not active

features.name: CoreInboundEmailRouting
features.description: Core module: routes inbound replies to tenant-generated emails back into the record that sent them, such as a Support ticket thread, independent of how the message arrives

actions.statement: Provision a unique inbound routing address under the platform's verified domain for every platform_shared tenant

Accept an inbound message from any intake entry point, such as a polled catch-all mailbox or a provider webhook, and normalise it into an InboundEmailDTO that carries the original recipient address before any other processing

enforce.expression: Every step after normalisation must behave identically regardless of which entry point delivered the message, so replacing or adding an entry point never changes the routing logic

actions.statement: Verify the message originates from a recognised source appropriate to its entry point, such as the platform's own authenticated mailbox connection or a provider's webhook signature
Process each inbound message at most once, identified by its Message-ID, so a re-polled mailbox or a retried webhook delivery never attaches a duplicate
Extract and verify the cryptographic signature embedded in the recipient sub-address before attempting any tenant lookup or matching logic

enforce.expression: An inbound email with a missing or invalid signature must be rejected outright and must never be matched by parsing the forgeable In-Reply-To or References headers alone

actions.statement: Resolve the tenant_id and originating record directly from the verified signature payload, not from message headers

enforce.expression: An inbound email that cannot be matched to a tenant-scoped record via a verified signature must never be attached to the wrong tenant's data

actions.statement: Dispatch an InboundEmailReceived event carrying the verified InboundEmailDTO so the owning module, such as Support, can append it to the correct thread

features.name: CoreExtensionPoints
features.description: Core module: the plugin-style hook registry that lets an installed module extend a Core UI screen, such as adding a tab to the customer profile, without ever modifying Core's own code

actions.statement: Publish each hook_name a Core screen exposes, such as CustomerProfileTabs or DashboardWidgets, at Core boot time
Let an installed module register a component_reference against an existing hook_name

enforce.expression: A module may only register into a hook_name that Core has explicitly published; it can never inject into an arbitrary point in another module's UI

actions.statement: Render every component registered for a hook_name in order_index sequence at runtime
Deregister a module's hook registrations automatically when that module is disabled for the tenant

features.name: CoreRecordExtensions
features.description: Core module: lets any installed module attach its own structured or semi-structured metadata to a Core record, such as a customer, without altering Core's schema

actions.statement: Validate core_entity refers to a table Core has explicitly opened for extension, such as customers or invoices
Store metadata as a JSON blob namespaced under module_key against the given core_entity_id

enforce.expression: A module must only read or write the metadata namespace registered to its own module_key, never another module's namespace

actions.statement: Return the merged core record plus every installed module's metadata namespace when the record is requested

features.name: CoreModuleDependencyRegistry
features.description: Core module: the explicit registry of hard prerequisite modules a given module requires before it can be enabled, preventing a chaotic web of implicit dependencies

actions.statement: Declare each module's hard prerequisites, for example a module requiring only Core, or requiring Core plus one specific named module

enforce.expression: Only Core may appear with an empty requires list; every other module must declare at least Core as a prerequisite

actions.statement: Expose the declared requires list to ModuleManager so it can validate an enable or disable action before applying it
Reject a declared dependency that would create a circular requirement between two modules

features.name: CoreTerminology
features.description: Core module: translates Core's generic internal entity names, such as Party or Contact, into the industry-specific language a tenant's business type expects, such as Customer, Patient, or Student

actions.statement: Store every Core entity under its most generic, universal name internally, such as Party, Account, or Contact
Resolve a display_term for each generic_term based on the tenant's business_type, falling back to the generic_term when no mapping is defined
Apply the resolved display_term across every module's UI labels and generated documents

enforce.expression: Renaming a generic_term for display must never rename or migrate the underlying Core table or column

features.name: CoreDashboardRegistry
features.description: Core module: the widget registration system that lets each installed module contribute dashboard widgets to an otherwise empty Core dashboard grid, without Core hardcoding any chart or metric

actions.statement: Let an installed module register a widget_id, widget_title, and default grid position when it activates for a tenant
Store the widget's data_endpoint, which must belong to the registering module, not Core

enforce.expression: The Core Dashboard must never query another module's database tables directly; every widget fetches its own data from its own data_endpoint

actions.statement: Assemble the tenant's dashboard by rendering every enabled module's registered widgets inside an empty grid container
Deregister a module's widgets automatically when that module is disabled for the tenant

features.name: CoreReportingPipeline
features.description: Core module: a standard time-series data pipeline that lets modules such as Financial and Support contribute data to a cross-module report without knowing about each other

actions.statement: Define a standard time-series schema of date, label, and value that every module maps its own metrics onto when asked
Maintain a tenant-scoped, indexed summary per module that pre-aggregates its metrics onto the standard schema, refreshed on a schedule appropriate to that metric
Query each active module's pre-aggregated view independently, filtered by tenant_id and the requested date range, rather than its live operational tables

enforce.expression: A cross-module report spanning a large date range must read from each module's pre-aggregated summary; an application-layer merge of independently fetched datasets is reserved for small result sets only, and a join across module-owned tables is never permitted

actions.statement: Merge the returned per-module series chronologically into a single overlay-ready series for the front end
Omit a module's series entirely, without erroring, if that module is not enabled for the tenant

features.name: CoreUsageMetering
features.description: Core module: measures each tenant's monthly usage of user seats, payments processed, and support tickets against the active plan's limits, receiving usage from other modules only through events and DTOs

actions.statement: Receive a UsageRecorded event carrying an immutable UsageRecordedDTO from the module that owns the metric, without Core calling that module
Add the amount to the tenant's counter for the current calendar month, creating the counter when it does not exist
Measure financial_volume in the tenant's billing currency
Count user_seats as the tenant's active workspace users, excluding customer portal users
Compare the counter to the limit allowed by the tenant's active plan, treating Enterprise as unlimited
Reject adding another active workspace user when it would exceed the plan's seat limit and prompt the tenant admin to upgrade

enforce.expression: The seat limit is a hard limit; the processed-volume and support-ticket limits must never reject or delete a payment or a ticket

actions.statement: Notify the tenant admin through CoreNotifications when a counter reaches 80 percent and again at 100 percent of its allowance
Show current usage against each limit on the tenant admin's subscription screen
Reset monthly counters at the start of each calendar month while keeping earlier months for reporting

features.name: FinancialTaxConfiguration
features.description: Financial module: tenant-configurable tax rates applied to quotations and invoices

actions.statement: Validate tax_name is not empty and tax_rate is a non-negative percentage
Create or update the tax rate scoped to the current tenant

enforce.expression: Only one tax rate per tenant may be marked as default at a time

actions.statement: Recalculate compound tax ordering when more than one compound tax rate is active

features.name: FinancialPaymentGatewayConfiguration
features.description: Financial module: lets a tenant admin enable Paysharp and Paystack and store the API credentials used to accept invoice payments

actions.statement: Verify the authenticated user has financial.settings.manage permission for this tenant
Validate the submitted api_key and api_secret against the gateway's test endpoint before saving

enforce.expression: Credentials must be validated with the gateway before is_enabled can be set to true

actions.statement: Encrypt and persist the credentials scoped to the current tenant
Allow more than one gateway to be enabled simultaneously so FinancialPaymentProcessing can offer a choice at checkout
Never expose a stored api_key or api_secret back to the frontend after saving; return only a masked reference

features.name: FinancialQuotations
features.description: Financial module: quotation lifecycle from draft through to conversion into an invoice

actions.statement: Look up the customer via CoreCustomerManagement and confirm customer_id belongs to the current tenant
Create a draft quotation with line items scoped to the current tenant and customer_id
Calculate line item totals, tax, and grand total using the tenant's FinancialTaxConfiguration rates
Transition the quotation through Draft, Sent, Accepted, and Declined in order

enforce.expression: A quotation must not be marked Accepted after its valid_until date has passed

actions.statement: Convert an Accepted quotation into a new Draft invoice, carrying forward the line items, tax, and customer_id

enforce.expression: Converting a quotation must never duplicate the customer's contact details onto the invoice; only customer_id is carried forward

actions.statement: Dispatch QuotationAccepted and QuotationConverted events

features.name: FinancialInvoicing
features.description: Financial module: invoice lifecycle, tax calculation, and branded PDF generation, fully tenant-scoped

actions.statement: Look up the customer via CoreCustomerManagement and confirm customer_id belongs to the current tenant

enforce.expression: The Financial module must reference the customer by customer_id only and must never store its own copy of customer contact details

actions.statement: Load the tenant's tax rates via FinancialTaxConfiguration and default currency via CoreSettings
Create or accept a converted-from-quotation invoice in Draft status with calculated totals
Transition the invoice through Draft, Approved, Sent, Part-Paid, Paid, Overdue, and Cancelled in order

enforce.expression: An invoice must not move to Paid unless its recorded paid_total meets or exceeds its total

actions.statement: Generate a branded PDF using CoreOrganisationProfile letterhead details, the customer's details from CoreCustomerManagement, and the CoreTheming colour palette
Send the invoice by email through CoreEmailIntegration
Register the Invoicing dashboard widget and reporting metrics with CoreDashboardRegistry and CoreReportingPipeline
Dispatch InvoiceCreated, InvoiceApproved, and InvoiceSent events for CoreNotifications to act on

features.name: FinancialPaymentProcessing
features.description: Financial module: records invoice payments taken through a tenant's configured Paysharp or Paystack gateway, or via manual EFT with an uploaded proof of payment

actions.statement: Verify invoice_id belongs to the current tenant and is not already fully paid
For paysharp or paystack, confirm a FinancialPaymentGatewayConfiguration is enabled for that gateway, then initiate a hosted payment session and redirect the customer to complete payment

enforce.expression: A gateway payment must never be initiated using a gateway the tenant has not enabled and validated

actions.statement: For eft, accept an uploaded proof_of_payment file and record the payment in a Pending Verification state

enforce.expression: An EFT payment must remain Pending Verification until a staff member with financial.payments.verify permission approves it

actions.statement: On gateway webhook confirmation, verify the payload signature before matching the transaction to its originating invoice

enforce.expression: A payment webhook must be signature-verified before any invoice balance is updated

actions.statement: Record the confirmed or verified payment against the invoice and update its paid_total

enforce.expression: paid_total must never exceed the invoice's total

actions.statement: Mark the invoice Paid once paid_total meets or exceeds total, or Part-Paid otherwise
Dispatch an InvoicePaid or PaymentRecorded event for CoreNotifications to act on

Dispatch a UsageRecorded event carrying an immutable UsageRecordedDTO with the recorded payment amount in the tenant's billing currency to the Core event bus so CoreUsageMetering can count processed volume

features.name: SupportCategoryManagement
features.description: Support module MVP: manages the Tier 2 subcategory lookup table beneath each fixed Tier 1 parent_category, so categories can be added, renamed, or soft-disabled without touching a hardcoded enum, and are automatically hidden when tied to a module the tenant has not enabled

actions.statement: Validate slug is snake_case and unique within its parent_category
Create or update the subcategory record with its parent_category, slug, and display_name
Soft-disable a subcategory by setting is_active to false rather than deleting it, preserving historical tickets that reference it

Hide a subcategory whose parent_category maps to a module the tenant has not enabled, such as billing_subscription mapping to Financial, by checking the tenant's active-modules list from ModuleManager

enforce.expression: A tenant must never be offered a subcategory tied to a module they have not enabled

actions.statement: Index subcategories by parent_category for fast cascading dropdown queries

features.name: SupportTicketManagement
features.description: Support module MVP: captures customer support requests via web form or email intake, classifies them by Tier 1 and Tier 2 category and impact, and tracks a simple chronological status through resolution; the schema is shaped to grow into full enterprise triage without breaking module boundaries

actions.statement: Identify the requesting user_id and tenant_id from the authenticated session before accepting the request
Look up the requester via CoreCustomerManagement, or create a new customer record there if the requester is unknown, and confirm customer_id belongs to the current tenant

enforce.expression: Support must reference the requester by customer_id only and must never store its own duplicate copy of their contact details

actions.statement: Validate subcategory_slug is an active SupportCategoryManagement entry under the given parent_category
Assign the ticket a unique reference and set its status to Open
Attach diagnostic metadata, such as browser logs, system version, or environment variables, through CoreRecordExtensions instead of a Support-owned column on the customer record
Track the ticket status in strict chronological order: Open, In Progress, Pending Engineering, Pending Customer, Resolved, and Closed

enforce.expression: A ticket must only move forward through its defined statuses, or back to In Progress from Pending Customer or Pending Engineering; it must never skip backward past Resolved

actions.statement: Register the Support dashboard widget and reporting metrics with CoreDashboardRegistry and CoreReportingPipeline
Dispatch a TicketCreated event carrying an immutable TicketCreatedDTO to the Core event bus so CoreNotifications can send the confirmation email
Dispatch a UsageRecorded event carrying an immutable UsageRecordedDTO for each created ticket to the Core event bus so CoreUsageMetering can count monthly tickets

features.name: SupportRoutingAndSla
features.description: Support module MVP: computes ticket priority from the tenant's subscription tier and selected impact, routes the ticket to its category's owning queue by parent_category, and stamps SLA response and resolution deadlines; workload-based assignment and proactive breach alerting are deferred post-launch, though the schema reserves the fields they will need

actions.statement: Evaluate the priority matrix by cross-referencing the tenant's subscription_plan against the selected impact, for example an Enterprise tenant reporting an entire department blocked resolves to Critical priority
Stamp sla_response_due_at and sla_resolution_due_at on the ticket based on the resolved priority

Route the ticket to its owning queue based on parent_category alone for the MVP, for example crm_modules to the Sales Tech Specialist queue, erp_modules to the Financial Modules Support queue, and billing_subscription directly to the Finance and Billing queue, bypassing technical support

enforce.expression: MVP routing selects a queue by parent_category only; workload-based agent assignment across a team is deferred post-launch

actions.statement: Pause the sla_resolution_due_at timer while the ticket is in Pending Customer status and resume it when the status returns to In Progress
Reserve, but do not yet actively alert on, an SLA breach threshold field so proactive breach notifications can be enabled post-launch without a schema change

features.name: SupportEngineeringEscalation
features.description: Support module MVP: lets an agent escalate a ticket identified as a genuine defect to the engineering team's issue tracker, keeping the ticket linked to the resulting bug card

actions.statement: Verify the escalating agent has support.tickets.escalate permission for this tenant
Transition the ticket to Pending Engineering status
Create a linked bug card in the engineering team's issue tracker, such as GitHub Issues, via its API and store the returned reference on the ticket

enforce.expression: A ticket must not be marked Pending Engineering unless a linked bug card reference is successfully stored

actions.statement: Notify the requesting customer that their issue has been escalated for engineering review

features.name: SupportResolutionAndClosure
features.description: Support module MVP: resolves a ticket with a root cause code, holds it in a soft-resolved verification window, and closes or reopens it based on customer response, finishing with a CSAT survey

actions.statement: Verify the ticket's status is In Progress or Pending Engineering before it can be resolved
Transition the ticket to Resolved and record the selected root_cause_code for reporting
Notify the customer that their ticket is resolved and start the verification_window_days grace period
Reopen the ticket to In Progress immediately if the customer replies within the verification window indicating the issue persists

enforce.expression: A customer reply during the verification window must reopen the ticket before the window can close it

actions.statement: Automatically transition the ticket to Closed once the verification window elapses with no customer reply
Dispatch a CSAT survey request through CoreNotifications once the ticket reaches Closed

features.name: SupportKnowledgeBase
features.description: Support module MVP: a simple CRUD system for internal and customer-facing articles and FAQs; automated ticket-deflection suggestions are deferred post-launch

actions.statement: Create, update, or archive the article scoped to the current tenant
Publish the article to the portal guard's help centre when is_customer_facing is true, or keep it staff-only otherwise

features.name: SupportCollaboration
features.description: Support module MVP: private internal notes and teammate mentions on a ticket, never visible to the requesting customer

actions.statement: Attach the note to the ticket's internal thread

enforce.expression: An internal note must never be exposed on the customer-facing portal view of the ticket

actions.statement: Notify each mentioned user via CoreNotifications

features.name: SupportReporting
features.description: Support module: performance metrics across ticket volume, response and resolution times, agent workload, root cause patterns, and customer satisfaction

actions.statement: Aggregate ticket volume, average first-response time, and average resolution time for the given date range
Compute per-agent workload and SLA breach counts
Aggregate ticket counts by root_cause_code to surface recurring defect patterns for the business
Compute the average customer satisfaction rating from post-resolution CSAT surveys
Map the aggregated metrics onto CoreReportingPipeline's standard date, label, and value schema when a cross-module report requests them

endpoints.name: CreateTenant
endpoints.description: Provisions a new tenant workspace on a wildcard subdomain during signup

actions.statement: Validate all required signup fields
Reject the request when the subdomain is taken or reserved, or when admin_email is already registered as a complete email address, never comparing the email domain
Create the tenant, admin user, and default settings on the requested wildcard subdomain
Activate the selected subscription plan with the chosen billing cycle and the billing currency derived from country_code
Issue a single-use login handoff URL on the tenant's subdomain for the new admin

returns.payload: A tenant with this subdomain or email address already exists

endpoints.name: MapCustomDomain
endpoints.description: Registers and verifies a custom domain to map over the tenant's wildcard subdomain

actions.statement: Verify the tenant's subscription plan permits custom domain mapping
Generate the CNAME target and TXT verification token
Store the domain in a pending verification state

returns.payload: Custom domain mapping is available on the Enterprise plan only
This domain is already mapped to another tenant

endpoints.name: SuspendTenant
endpoints.description: Control plane: suspends a tenant's data-plane access without deleting their data

actions.statement: Verify the authenticated user is an operator staff member with control_plane.tenants.suspend permission
Update the tenant's status to suspended in TenantRegistry
Notify the tenant admin that their workspace has been suspended

endpoints.name: PlatformBillingWebhook
endpoints.description: Control plane: receives subscription and payment events from the connected billing processor

actions.statement: Verify the signature against the processor's stored webhook secret

enforce.expression: A billing webhook with an invalid or missing signature must be rejected before any subscription state changes

actions.statement: Match the payload to its originating tenant
Update the tenant's subscription status and trigger SubscriptionManagement to recompute access

returns.payload: No matching tenant found for this billing event

endpoints.name: UpdateTheme
endpoints.description: Persists the tenant's colour palette and returns it for immediate application

actions.statement: Verify the authenticated user has core.settings.manage permission for this tenant
Validate colour values and contrast ratios
Persist the palette via CoreSettings

endpoints.name: ListNotifications
endpoints.description: Returns the current user's recent notifications and unread count

actions.statement: Load the authenticated user's most recent notifications scoped to the current tenant
Compute the unread_count

endpoints.name: UpdateOrganisationProfile
endpoints.description: Creates or updates the tenant's own organisation profile used on branded documents

actions.statement: Verify the authenticated user has core.settings.manage permission for this tenant
Validate organisation_name and organisation_email
Persist the organisation profile scoped to the tenant

returns.payload: Missing permission to manage the organisation profile

endpoints.name: ConfigureEmailIntegration
endpoints.description: Configures how the tenant's outbound and inbound email is handled

actions.statement: Verify the authenticated user has core.settings.manage permission for this tenant
Validate email_provider is permitted under the tenant's subscription plan
Initiate the Microsoft 365 Admin Consent flow or test the custom SMTP connection as applicable
Persist the configuration scoped to the current tenant

returns.payload: Missing permission or plan is not Enterprise

endpoints.name: StoreCustomer
endpoints.description: Creates or updates a customer in the tenant's shared customer directory

actions.statement: Verify the authenticated user has core.customers.manage permission for this tenant
Validate customer_name and email
Create or update the customer record scoped to the current tenant
Dispatch a CustomerCreated or CustomerUpdated event

endpoints.name: UpdateRecordMetadata
endpoints.description: Lets an installed module read or write its own metadata namespace on a Core record without altering Core's schema

actions.statement: Verify the requesting module_key matches the module making the request

enforce.expression: A module may only write to its own metadata namespace on the record

actions.statement: Validate core_entity is open for extension
Persist the metadata JSON blob under the module's namespace against core_entity_id

returns.payload: This module may not write to another module's metadata namespace

endpoints.name: ListDashboardWidgets
endpoints.description: Returns the current tenant's assembled dashboard grid from every enabled module's registered widgets

actions.statement: Load every widget registered by an enabled module via CoreDashboardRegistry for the current tenant
Return each widget's id, title, data_endpoint, and grid position without fetching its data

endpoints.name: GetCrossModuleReport
endpoints.description: Returns a merged, chronologically overlaid time-series report across every enabled module that contributes the requested metric

actions.statement: Determine which enabled modules contribute data for metric_key
Query each contributing module's own reporting endpoint independently via CoreReportingPipeline
Merge the returned series chronologically into a single payload

returns.payload: No enabled module contributes the requested metric_key

endpoints.name: ConfigurePaymentGateway
endpoints.description: Enables a payment gateway and stores its API credentials for the current tenant

actions.statement: Verify the authenticated user has financial.settings.manage permission for this tenant
Validate the credentials against the gateway's test endpoint
Encrypt and persist the credentials scoped to the current tenant

returns.payload: Missing permission to manage payment gateways
The supplied credentials could not be validated with the gateway

endpoints.name: StoreQuotation
endpoints.description: Creates a new quotation for the current tenant

actions.statement: Verify the authenticated user has financial.quotations.create permission for this tenant
Validate customer_id exists in Core's shared customer directory and belongs to the current tenant
Create the quotation in Draft status with calculated totals

endpoints.name: ConvertQuotation

enforce.expression: Only a quotation in Accepted status may be converted to an invoice

returns.payload: Only an accepted quotation can be converted to an invoice

endpoints.name: StoreInvoice
endpoints.description: Creates a new invoice for the current tenant

actions.statement: Verify the authenticated user has financial.invoices.create permission for this tenant
Validate customer_id exists in Core's shared customer directory and belongs to the current tenant
Create the invoice in Draft status with calculated totals

endpoints.name: InitiateInvoicePayment
endpoints.description: Starts a payment against an invoice via a tenant's configured Paysharp or Paystack gateway, or manual EFT with a proof of payment upload

actions.statement: Verify invoice_id belongs to the current tenant and is not already fully paid
For paysharp or paystack, confirm the gateway is enabled via FinancialPaymentGatewayConfiguration, then create a hosted payment session and return its gateway_redirect_url
For eft, store the uploaded proof_of_payment file and set status to Pending Verification

returns.payload: Missing permission to pay this invoice, or the selected gateway is not enabled
This invoice is already fully paid

endpoints.name: PaymentGatewayWebhook
endpoints.description: Receives asynchronous payment confirmation callbacks from Paysharp or Paystack

actions.statement: Verify the signature against the tenant's stored gateway secret

enforce.expression: A webhook with an invalid or missing signature must be rejected before any data is written

actions.statement: Match the payload to its originating invoice and tenant
Record the payment and update the invoice's paid_total and status

returns.payload: No matching invoice found for this payment

endpoints.name: VerifyEftPayment
endpoints.description: Lets a staff member approve a manually submitted EFT proof of payment

actions.statement: Verify the authenticated user has financial.payments.verify permission for this tenant
Confirm the payment is currently in Pending Verification status

actions.statement: Mark the payment verified and update the invoice's paid_total and status

returns.payload: This payment is not awaiting verification

endpoints.name: StoreCategory
endpoints.description: Creates or updates a Tier 2 subcategory beneath a fixed Tier 1 parent_category

actions.statement: Verify the authenticated user has support.categories.manage permission for this tenant
Validate slug is snake_case and unique within its parent_category
Create or update the subcategory scoped to the current tenant

endpoints.name: ListCategories
endpoints.description: Returns active Tier 2 subcategories for cascading dropdowns, optionally filtered by a Tier 1 parent_category

Exclude any subcategory whose parent_category maps to a module the tenant has not enabled

endpoints.name: StoreTicket
endpoints.description: Creates a new support ticket for the current tenant using the relational Tier 1 and Tier 2 category structure

Validate subcategory_slug is an active SupportCategoryManagement entry under parent_category
Create the ticket in Open status with the given priority computed via SupportRoutingAndSla
Route the ticket via SupportRoutingAndSla

endpoints.name: ClaimTicket

Confirm the ticket is currently Open

actions.statement: Assign the ticket to the claiming agent and transition it to In Progress

returns.payload: This ticket has already been claimed

endpoints.name: ReplyToTicket
endpoints.description: Appends a threaded reply to a ticket from either an agent or the requesting customer, updating its status accordingly

actions.statement: Append the message to the ticket's threaded history
Transition the ticket to Pending Customer when an agent's reply requests more information
Transition the ticket back to In Progress, resuming the SLA resolution timer, when the customer replies

endpoints.name: EscalateTicket
endpoints.description: Escalates a ticket identified as a genuine defect to the engineering team's issue tracker

actions.statement: Verify the authenticated user has support.tickets.escalate permission for this tenant
Create the linked bug card in the engineering issue tracker and transition the ticket to Pending Engineering

endpoints.name: ResolveTicket
endpoints.description: Resolves a ticket with a root cause code and starts the customer verification window

actions.statement: Verify the authenticated user has support.tickets.resolve permission for this tenant
Confirm the ticket's status is In Progress or Pending Engineering

actions.statement: Transition the ticket to Resolved, record root_cause_code, and start the verification window
